title: The naive framing: "does Claude predict which deals close?"
text: Someone assumed the forecast skill predicts which deals will actually close. It doesn't, it weighs them. So, does Clod predict which deals close or just weigh the odds?

title: Pipeline becomes a number
text: Forecast turns your pipeline into one number. You hand it deals name, amount, stage, close date, plus your quota. Each stage carries a default probability. Negotiation 80%, discovery 20. Multiply amount by probability stage by stage and add it up. That sum is the weighted forecast. Take one deal from that

title: One deal, weighed (the anchor)
text: Pipeline, Acme Corp, $50,000 negotiation, closing January 31st. At 80% it adds 40,000 to the weighted forecast. Confident enough to sit in commit, the deals you'd stake your number on. Lower confidence deals go in a separate pile, upside. One flag,

title: The one flag: your own data
text: Connect your CRM and those stage probabilities stop being defaults. The skill pulls your pipeline automatically, uses your team's actual historical win rates instead, and tracks how the forecast moves over time. Until then, every probability above is a generic assumption. Back to Acme Corp, no

title: Commit can still slip
text: Activity in 14 days flags it for a re-engage, even though it's sitting in commit. A committed deal isn't a closed deal, it's just the one you'd bet on, and the bet can still go wrong.

title: Low odds can still land
text: The other direction holds, too. A discovery stage deal at 20% isn't written off, it can still close, it's just not what you plan around. And the gap analysis only tells you how far short of quota you are. It never tells you which deals will close it. The

title: Carry-out
text: Forecast weighs probability, not certainty. A stage weighted number tells you how big your pipeline is, never which deals inside it will actually close.

title: Your turn
text: Your turn, paste this into Clod. Here's my pipeline. Acme Corp, $50,000 in negotiation, closing this month. Tech Start, $25,000 in discovery. My quota is 100,000 this quarter. Give me a weighted forecast, best likely, and worst case, split into commit versus upside, and flag anything at risk. That's the actual test of what a forecast promises and what it doesn't. Weighed, not predicted.
